name: AppLayout
label: App layout
description: Full-page template pairing the collapsible App sidebar with a content area, in one of the three app shell modes: flush, floating or inset.

props.name: activeTertiaryKey
props.description: Active third-level item key, listed in the sidebar's side panel

props.name: subNav
props.description: Where sub-items show: the sidebar's accordion, or straight into its side panel (see AppSidebar)

props.name: children
props.description: Page content — centred in the main area

props.name: layout
props.description:
How the rail and the content meet the page, one of the three app shell
modes. `flush` (the default) runs the rail edge to edge on the shell
colour behind a hairline, the content centred beside it on the crisp
app surface, nothing raised. `floating` floats the rail as a glass card,
the content still centred. `inset` runs the rail flush on the shell
colour and sets the content full width in a raised surface (hairline
and floating shadow) inset from the other edges, which scrolls inside
itself.

props.name: theme
props.description:
Colour scheme: 'dark' pins the layout to the dark theme (the historical
behaviour and the default); 'inherit' drops the pin so the layout
follows the surrounding data-theme like any other component.

props.name: linkComponent
props.description:
The component its links render with, such as Next.js's `Link`, so they
navigate through the app's router; passed on to the AppSidebar rail. Wins over a
LinkProvider's; a plain `<a>` when neither is set.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional CSS classes on outer wrapper

AppSidebarLayout.description: The three app shell modes, how the rail meets the page: edge to edge behind a hairline, floating as a card, or flush beside a raised inset surface.

LinkComponent.description: A component that renders a link in place of a plain `<a>`, such as a router's.

LinkComponentProps.description:
The props a link component receives: every anchor attribute, the ref, and
an `href` that is always a string. Next.js's `Link` takes these as they
are; a router whose link takes `to` instead needs a one-line adapter:
`({ href, ...props }) => <RouterLink to={href} {...props} />`.
